reason: The quote states presigned URLs grant time-limited access to objects without updating the bucket policy and use the credentials of the IAM principal who generated the URL; displays are verbatim.

The quotes state a presigned URL allows an upload without the other party having AWS credentials or permissions, that an existing object with the same key is replaced, and that the bucket owner owns the object after upload.
The quote states there is no minimum charge and lists the same six cost components as the claim.
Read together, the quotes list data transferred in from the internet as an exception to paying for all bandwidth into and out of S3.
The quote supports the first 100GB per month free aggregated across all AWS services and Regions except China and GovCloud, but the scope qualifier adds per account, which the quote does not state.

Under the list of exceptions to paying for bandwidth, the quotes name transfer from a bucket to any AWS service in the same Region (including a different account) and transfer between buckets in the same Region.

The quotes support that data transferred out to CloudFront is an exception to bandwidth charges, but the claim adds advice (a reason to put CloudFront in front of a bucket with many downloads) that the quotes do not state.

The quote supports per-request ingest charges for PUT, COPY or lifecycle moves into any class and says to consider the cost, but the claim adds that transitioning many small objects can cost more than it saves, which the quote does not say.
The quote states a monthly monitoring and automation charge per object in Intelligent-Tiering, no retrieval charges and no additional tiering charges when objects move between tiers.
The quote states LIST requests for any class are charged at the S3 Standard PUT, COPY and POST rate and that DELETE and CANCEL requests are free.

The quote supports paying for both the archive at its Glacier rate and the temporary copy at the S3 Standard rate, but says for a duration of time you choose; the claim's unit (number of days) is not in the quote.

The quote supports retrieval charges on GET for Standard-IA, One Zone-IA and Glacier Instant Retrieval and as part of the restore for Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive, but the scope qualifier per GB retrieved is not stated in the quote.
The quote states the storage rate depends on object size, how long objects were stored during the month, and the storage class.
The quote states buckets and objects are private and accessible only with explicitly granted permissions, managed with bucket policies, IAM policies, ACLs and S3 Access Points.

The quotes support the ACL rule and that S3 starts by assuming a policy is public; the fixed-value list is only in the context, which does not show aws:SourceVpc or aws:SourceVpce, and the claim drops the note that very broad aws:SourceIp ranges are still evaluated as public.
The quote states some but not all quotas can be increased and increases are not granted immediately, possibly taking a couple of days.

Under what is not replicated, the quote names Flexible Retrieval, Deep Archive and the Intelligent-Tiering Archive and Deep Archive Access tiers and says they cannot be replicated until restored and copied to a different class.
Under updates to bucket-level subresources, the quote states lifecycle or notification changes on the source are not applied to the destination, allowing different configurations.
In the cross-account scenario the quotes state the destination owner must grant the source owner replication permissions with a bucket policy and that destination buckets cannot be Requester Pays.

The quotes say you can replicate delete markers if delete marker replication is enabled, with the both-buckets effect and no support for tag-based rules; they do not say delete markers are replicated only when it is enabled, so the claim's only goes beyond the quote.
The quota row with its header gives a default of 28, Adjustable Yes, described as destination buckets per source bucket across all replication rules.
The quote states replication can put objects directly into Flexible Retrieval, Deep Archive or another class, or replicate to the same class and use destination lifecycle rules to move them colder.

The quotes and context support KMS request quotas applying to replication requests and ThrottlingException, but the scope qualifier per account, per Region is not stated (context mentions only the AWS account).
The quotes state replication time depends on size and can take several hours for large objects, and destination lifecycle rules honor the original creation time, not the replica arrival.

The quotes state metadata replicates source to replica only by default, and with replica modification sync enabled on both buckets replica changes go back to the source (two-way); the context names tags, ACLs and Object Lock settings.
The quote states that if the source bucket has Object Lock enabled, the destination buckets must also have it enabled.
The quote states S3 can change replica ownership to the destination bucket owner regardless of source object owner, called owner override, usable to restrict access to replicas.

The quote supports CRR inter-Region data transfer out per destination Region and the RTC data transfer and metrics charges, but the scope qualifier per GB replicated is not in the quote and does not fit the metrics charge.
The quotes state SSE-S3, SSE-KMS and DSSE-KMS replicas use the source encryption type, not the destination default, and unencrypted source objects get the destination bucket default encryption.
Under what S3 does not replicate by default, the quotes give the A to B to C example and say to use Batch Replication for replicas.

The quotes state up to five GET/HEAD and one PUT to the source and one PUT per destination per object, that these count toward request rate guidelines, and that you pay for only one PUT per object replicated.
The quotes support versioning on both buckets and that S3 must have permissions to replicate on your behalf, but the claim's parenthetical (an IAM role) is not stated in the quotes or context.

The quotes state both buckets must have versioning enabled, disabling it on the destination makes replication fail, and disabling it on the source returns an error until the replication configuration is removed.

Under granting permissions for the IAM role, the quotes require kms:Decrypt on the source key and kms:Encrypt on the replica key, and the key owner in another account must grant them to the account that owns the role.
The quota row with its header gives 1,000, Adjustable No, described as the maximum number of rules in a replication configuration.
The quotes and context state replication supports SSE-C objects, needs no extra SSE-C permissions beyond those already required, and has no additional charges.

The quotes state SSE-KMS and DSSE-KMS objects are not replicated by default and you explicitly opt in; the context under the same heading says to add the customer managed KMS key ID used to encrypt replicas.
The quotes state that with tag-based rules and live replication the tag must be set in PutObject, objects tagged later are not replicated, and S3 Batch Replication must be used for them.
The quotes state most objects in seconds and 99.99% within 15 minutes by design, an SLA of 99.9% within 15 minutes per Region pair per billing month, and enablement per replication rule.
The quote states to use two-way replication rules before configuring Multi-Region Access Point failover controls so data written to the failover bucket replicates back to the source.
